name: Monster Trainer Monster Auror
body:
Monster aurors are not monster trainers in a traditional sense.

They often view the capture of monsters as a form of slavery, and prefer instead to draw their magic from an internal well of power—in this case, their essence. A monster auror does not travel the Kingdom to capture monsters, but instead to learn how to adjust his essence to gain their abilities for his own use.

Monster Training

A monster auror begins play with one monster he has been given by another trainer, such as a monster researcher. This monster is considered the auror’s primary monster. At 2nd level, and every level thereafter, the auror can allow his primary monster to grow, if able, or choose a new primary monster from the common monsters to which he has access (different areas have different common monsters, as detailed in Chapter 4). He can also trade his primary monster with another trainer, provided the monster he receives has a CR equal to or lower than his monster trainer level.

Finally, a monster auror can still accept willing creatures into his essence and call upon them in the same way any trainer could, but these monsters do not change the trainer’s spells known (see below). This alters monster training and replaces capture monster.

Spellcasting

Each monster auror begins play with the ability to tap into his own essence to cast spells. He gains spells known as a sorcerer of his level, and the spells he can learn are drawn from his primary monster’s trainer spell list. If he chooses to change his primary monster upon gaining a level, the auror can decide to learn new spells from either the original monster or his new primary monster.

Starting Characters Above 1st Level

A monster’s value to its trainer is equal to its CR squared x 500 gp. When starting a monster trainer above 1st level, use this guideline to effectively “purchase” monsters you have captured up to this point in your adventures. This does not mean you can buy monsters at any time or sell monsters you’ve captured in game; it only reflects their value as an aid when building a new character, and you should still work with your GM to determine how you acquired the monsters you do start with. Upon reaching 4th level, and at every even-numbered monster trainer level after that (6th, 8th, and so on), an auror can choose to learn a new spell in place of one he already knows. In effect, the auror loses the old spell in exchange for the new one. The new spell’s level must be the same as that of the spell being exchanged. An auror may swap only a single spell at any given level, and must choose whether or not to swap the spell at the same time that he gains new spells known for the level.

This alters the monster trainer’s spellcasting ability.

Alter Essence (Sp)

At 1st level, a monster auror learns how to alter his essence to mimic the monsters with whom he interacts. Once per day, after witnessing a monster cast a spell or use one of its spell-like, supernatural, or extraordinary abilities, the auror can use a standard action within 1 minute to add that ability to his list of spells known until the next time he regains spells. At 3rd level, and every 4 levels thereafter, the auror can use alter essence one additional time per day.

The effective spell level of an ability gained with alter essence is equal to a spell of the same name, or half the CR of the monster using it (minimum 1) if no such spell exists. If the equivalent spell exists at different levels, the auror uses the highest level at which it could be gained.

Abilities with limited uses (1/day, every 1d4 rounds, etc…) are similarly limited for the auror, in addition to requiring a spell slot.

Any ability learned with alter essence counts as a spell when used by the auror and uses the auror’s Charisma modifier in place of another (a breath weapon typically uses Constitution, for example). Abilities gained more than once do not stack. Constant abilities last a number of hours equal to the auror’s monster trainer level before they must be cast again.

Abilities with no spell equivalent are mimicked exactly as they were used, except that any save DCs are replaced by the auror’s spell save DC for the level used to cast them.

Alter essence replaces eschew materials, talented trainer, swap monster, and the trainer perk gained at 19th level.

Echoes of Magic (Sp)

At 3rd level, a monster auror learns how to pattern a small number of abilities he has learned with alter essence so that he can recall them after resting. When he uses alter essence, the auror can now choose to learn or pattern an ability he would gain. He can pattern up to a maximum number of abilities equal to his Charisma modifier + 1/2 his level (minimum 1). Once a monster auror has patterned his maximum number of abilities, he cannot pattern more unless he gives up one of those he has already.

Each morning, when the auror regains his spells, he can expend uses of alter essence to relearn an ability he has patterned, adding it to his list of spells known for the day. This replaces spell familiarity and channel monster.

Trainer Perks

The following perks complement the auror: Beloved monster, downtime ally, evasion, stalwart, tactics training, tough command, and uncanny dodge.
